intro:
This file answers three questions about the SystemVerilog tier of lean-surfaces (ls-sv): **what does it refuse today**,
**what is meant to be allowed later (and what has to exist first)**, and **what will never be allowed (and which principle says so)**.

It is generated from [`docs/sv-refusals.json`](sv-refusals.json) by `tools/gen_sv_refusals.py` and checked against the code by
`python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --check`: a tagged refusal in the extractor or the Lean code that is missing from the data, or a
listed tag that has disappeared from the code, fails the check. The svGolf-facing twin, for contestants and task authors, is
`svgolf/REFUSALS.md`, generated from the same data. It lives with the svGolf project (the golf branch), so the paths under `svgolf/`
cited in this file are absent from a checkout without it.

A refusal is a LOUD `Unsupported` node (extractor) or a loud process / expression / elaboration error (Lean) or a loader gate: the
design either loads with a defined meaning or it does not load. Nothing here is silently approximated. The long reasons live in the
per-topic documents linked at the end (`docs/sv-*.md`); this register is the index and the classification.
scope_note:
The register classifies each refusal for the **ls-sv semantics tier** (the `category` of the row). The charter rules the tier's endgame to be
the whole specification, including the verification tier (classes, constrained randomization, assertions) and the full clause-4 scheduler
([docs/sv-charter.md](sv-charter.md) sections 6.3, 6.4, 6.6), so a construct can be `later` for ls-sv and still be unacceptable in a
**svGolf submission**, whose scored artifact is a combinational Yosys netlist. Where the two differ the row carries a second line
`svGolf: ...` (the field `svgolf` in the data). Delays, randomness, classes, strings and reals are the typical cases: `later` in the
semantics, `never` for a golf submission (principles `P-NO-TIME`, `P-SYNTHESIZABLE`).

categories.refused-now: refused loudly today and this is the intended behaviour at this version; no future is recorded
categories.later: refused today and intended to be ALLOWED once a stated prerequisite is met (a proof obligation, a model extension, a checker stage, a measured benefit); the row names the prerequisite and, where recorded, the plan item
categories.never: refused by principle and not to be allowed: no meaning can be given that is the same for the proof (ls-sv / slang) and the score (Yosys netlist), or it is not synthesizable hardware, or it would let the proved design differ from the scored one; the row names the principle
categories.refused-pending: decided and in flight, not yet in the code (transitional): the row names the decision; the completeness check allows its tag to be absent and warns once it appears

principles.text: Proof and score read ONE program: a construct the two frontends (slang for the proof, Yosys for the score) read differently, that slang rejects, or that Yosys cannot read, cannot be admitted.
No construct whose meaning is a synthesis-tool directive: pragmas, attributes, `ifdef SYNTHESIS / YOSYS, translate_off comments.
No delays, timing, wall-clock or time-dependent behaviour in a combinational task: synthesis ignores them, so the proved (timed) behaviour and the scored netlist would differ.
Not synthesizable hardware: classes, dynamic memory, strings, reals, file I/O, fork/join, program blocks, DPI; the scored artifact is a Yosys gate netlist.
The tools split (Icarus, Xcelium, Verilator, Yosys, slang give different values for the same text) and no consistent reading exists: refuse loudly, never decide for one side.
Nondeterministic or scheduling-dependent results: a combinational result must be a function of the inputs, whatever the schedule.

(added by the register authors, to confirm) The evidence a verdict rests on (checker, trusted statement, generated Goal, axiom set, toolchain) must not be changeable by the submission; a proof is accepted by the kernel from the allowed axioms alone.

policies.policy: Combinational tasks only for now; sequential tasks (serial multiplier, iterative divider) and the sequential task statement are deferred.
policies.source: memory svgolf-project (Thomas 2026-10-29: 'keep things combinatorial to begin with'); svgolf/PLAN.md Task ladder, Day 6

policies.policy: Refuse where the tools split: where Icarus, Xcelium, Verilator, Yosys and slang differ on the same text, or the model would follow one oracle against explicit LRM text, refuse LOUDLY. Refusal-only rounds: a fix may add a loud refusal, revert to HEAD, or correct a value only where Icarus, the Yosys netlist and slang agree; nothing becomes newly admitted. Over-refusal is accepted over a silent wrong value.
policies.source: docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md section 6 ('The policy (Thomas)'); memory xcelium-access; svgolf/PLAN.md Round 5

policies.policy: Xcelium is the reference simulator when building ls-sv (model differs => model suspect); Icarus, Verilator, mox are witnesses. Xcelium is not infallible: where it departs from explicit LRM text and the others follow the LRM, refuse. Xcelium is never required by CI or the svGolf checker: its results are pinned data (harness/sv/xcelium_golden.json, default flags, no -ii_val).

Icarus-only splits (Icarus departs from the LRM while Xcelium, Yosys and the model agree) are DECLARED departures (hash-bound `oracle_disagreement` rows in harness/sv/cases2.json), not refusals; Icarus is an optional 4-state witness.
policies.source: docs/sv-oracle-disagreements.md; docs/sv-xcelium-audit.md 6.1 item 9 (relayed by the lead as recorded; no verbatim Thomas sentence found in the docs)

policies.policy: unique / unique0 / priority carry proof obligations; v0 refuses them; the proof-obligation encoding (WP5) is deferred past v0.
x/z literals and the fourstate stage stay in v0; the x-taint feature (allow x sources, forbid x-tainted values reaching non-monotone decisions) comes later.

Contestants may add missing SV features to ls-sv by PR; Thomas approves every such PR. A feature PR carries differential cases against independent oracles; where the construct brings an x source, a rule in svgolf/score/fourstate.py lands first.
policies.source: memory svgolf-project (2026-10-28); svgolf/PLAN.md Decisions; svgolf/README.md Rules

policies.policy: No restrictions on the SV a player may write beyond the per-task operator banlist and the safety gates (source gate, 4-state rules, one-driver rule, Unclocked). A disagreement between ls-sv and Yosys on the same text is a bug report we want, surfaced by the post-synthesis check; known ones are nevertheless refused statically.

The operator banlist is per task: it bans the run-time operator that IS the task plus what Yosys merges into the same cell (alumacc: `+ - *` share cells). Constant arithmetic and comparisons stay allowed; whether comparisons should stay allowed in the `add` task is an open policy question.
policies.source: memory svgolf-project (2026-10-27); svgolf/README.md The banlist; svgolf/tasks/add/README.md

policies.policy: Proofs are symbolic and parametric (for all N); bv_decide only for fixed-size subgoals and only once the checker can verify it; only the task's allowed axioms; native_decide is banned in svGolf submissions (the lean-surfaces proof lanes follow the separate 2026-08-22 ruling: discouraged, not banned).
policies.source: memory svgolf-project (2026-10-27); svgolf/README.md Rules; AGENTS.md Never

policies.policy: svGolf stays separate from lean-surfaces (no svGolf entries in lakefile.toml or LeanModels.lean); general ls-sv work goes to LeanModels/Sv and is merged to main.

Refusal LOCI differ and a register must cover all of them: (a) extractor Unsupported kinds; (b) Lean-side unsupported processes / Except errors inside `name.sem`; (c) guards BESIDE `name.sem`, run by `load_design_sv2` (defaults and every probe-sidecar point), the runner and the `*Report` functions, because the instantiation lemmas are stated for the unguarded family; (d) svGolf checker stages. A proof about `name.sem` at a point no consumer checks is not covered by guards of kind (c).
policies.source: LeanModels/Sv/RangeGuard2.lean header; CombAlias2.lean; docs/sv-charter.md WP4 and CX

policies.policy: A refusal on either side of a cross-check is never agreement; stages fail closed (unconfirmed / refused / frontendRejects verdicts; postsynth rejects incomplete runs or x/z in ls-sv outputs).

schema: entries[] (ls-sv tier) and svgolf.entries[] (svGolf checker) share one record shape:

id (unique slug), tag (display name; `Family:detail` where the code has one), group, layers (extractor | lean-model | lean-guard | lean-loader | lean-proof-tooling | svgolf-*), trigger (a measured source, `H:` = the body of the standard test module), why, category (refused-now | later | never | refused-pending), proposed (true = not confirmed by Thomas), decided_by (the recorded decision), since (date, when known).

later: prerequisite (required) and plan (a plan_items id); never: principle (required, from the principle table); refused-pending: decided_by or source (the decision) and kinds that may be absent from the code.
svgolf (optional, on an ls-sv entry): {category, principle | prerequisite, proposed}: the status for a svGolf submission when it differs from the ls-sv status.

kinds.extractor / kinds.lean: the code tags the row covers (exact strings; `glob:<pattern>` for a deliberate family; `@default:<function>` for an extractor site that takes the slang class name; a bare `*` for a site whose whole kind is built at run time). The completeness check requires every live code tag to be covered and every listed tag to exist.

match: [{file, text}]: for a refusal that has only a message, the text must still be found in the file. where: [{file, fn}]: the function that raises it (line numbers are resolved by --where, never stored). attacks: svgolf only, `task/name` of every tests/expected.json design the row explains.

evidence (where it is documented), unverified (read from the source, never triggered by a run), verified_by_run, notes, value_rank / value_note (the ordering of the 'Allowed later' table), aggregate (svGolf only: a summary row hidden from svgolf/REFUSALS.md).

It stays loud in a parameter default, a localparam or a generate condition: the constant tier has its own width rules for `~` (an INT-class `~` is refused there) and the lowering was not measured against them.
entries.prerequisite: a measured width rule for `~` / `^` in the constant tier (Param.lean `evalInt` refuses an INT-class `~`; `evalSized` has the sized case), then the same lowering in constant positions
entries.evidence: extractors/sv/test_xnor_lowering.py; cases2.json rows xnor_bin*, xnor_red*, xnor_seq, xnor_sgn*, xnor_n* (Icarus + pinned Xcelium) and the refusal rows xnor_sgn_wide, xnor_const, xnor_genconst; Examples/system-verilog/xnor_n (every-width Table 11-14 proof); Examples/system-verilog/sem2/xnor_*; docs/sv-xnor.md (M0 tier)
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-29: approved the refused-now and later classifications of the register
entries.notes: WP-L2 (2026-10-30): binary `~^` / `^~` SUPPORTED in signal expressions (extractor lowering, differential rows against Icarus and pinned Xcelium, an every-width hand proof, this register); the reduction `~^a` was already admitted and is pinned by rows now. A signed operand PAIR assigned to a wider target stays the loud `ConversionExpression:width` (the tier has no signed widening; `^` refuses the same text). The sv_comb tactics do NOT read it: the recognizer rejects every unary operator (`~`), which is WP-G's item; once `~` is in the fragment `~(a ^ b)` needs no further change. The M0 (self-check) tier is untouched.

entries.why: The extractor never emits a select whose width or offset disagrees with the type the compiler resolved, or with the element width the semantic tier reads the select's base with (`Param2.elemOf`): the select lowering ends in a guard that turns any such node into this loud kind. `a[1][1]` over a three-dimensional 2-state array was lowered to a BitSel of a BitSel, which the tier reads as ONE bit of `a[1]` where Xcelium reads the 4-bit element (silently wrong before the guard). Also the net under the member-select lowering (a window outside, or of another width than, the selected elements).
entries.decided_by: WP-E1 2026-10-30: refuse rather than emit a window the compiler's type contradicts (lead review pending)
entries.notes: Measured 2026-10-30: bit [1:0][1:0][3:0] a, y = a[1][1]: Xcelium 24.03-s004 gives 1010 for a = 1010011001011100, the pre-guard model 0001. A 4-state `logic` array of the same shape takes the ArraySel path and is unaffected; supporting the 2-state shape is open (no plan item).

svgolf.intro:
svGolf asks for two things about each design you submit: a Lean proof that it meets the task's trusted statement under the ls-sv
semantics, and a score from a pinned Yosys flow. The checker refuses a design or a proof when the proof and the score could be about
different circuits, or when the evidence could be forged. This document lists every refusal the checker makes, why, and what you
can write instead, then says which refusals are meant to go away and which never will.

It has two halves that are easy to confuse. **The checker's own stages** (source gate, banlist, fourstate, statement, axioms, score,
post-synthesis check) are described below stage by stage. **The language tier** (`ls-sv`, the semantics your proof is about) refuses
more constructs than the checker does; those show up as `extract` or `design` failures and are summarised near the end and listed in
full in `docs/sv-refusals.md` of the lean-surfaces repository.

This file is generated from `docs/sv-refusals.json` of lean-surfaces by `tools/gen_sv_refusals.py` and is written to be read without
the rest of that repository: links to lean-surfaces documents are given as repository paths.

stages.refuses: unknown keys, a status other than ready / draft, a `ready` task without a reference proof

stages.what: checks the Lean file's imports against an allowlist
stages.refuses: any import outside Init, Std, Lean, LeanModels.Sv.*, SvGolf.*, tasks.*, spec.*, Submission.Design; a second file; `module` / `prelude` headers

stages.what: `score/srcgate.py`: makes the proved program and the scored program ONE text and strips every comment
stages.refuses: preprocessor directives, attributes, synthesis-pragma comments, `unique` / `unique0` / `priority`, x/z/? literal digits, odd characters

stages.what: the pinned lean-surfaces extractor reads the canonical text
stages.refuses: whatever the extractor refuses (the language tier), a wrong top module, a parameter list that differs from the task's

stages.what: `score/banlist.py`: pyslang front check plus a Yosys backstop
stages.refuses: the run-time operators the task bans, in every disguise Yosys turns into the same cell
any way an x or z value can arise: constants with unknown bits, out-of-range selects, undriven or conflicting nets, logic loops, latches

stages.what: builds the trusted svGolf modules and the ls-sv evaluator (not timed)

stages.refuses: loader refusals: cross-checks against slang, the one-driver rule, self-reading `always_comb`, select guards, the multi-point probe check

stages.what: compiles `Solution.lean` under the task's time limit
stages.refuses: a proof that does not compile in time

stages.what: snapshots the trusted files before and after the solution builds
stages.refuses: a solution whose build changes a staged or trusted file (a tripwire, not a sandbox)
a missing theorem, a proof of another statement, axioms outside the task's set, `extern` / `implemented_by`

stages.what: kernel replay of the submission's modules
stages.refuses: declarations added with the kernel check switched off

stages.what: `score/score.py`: the two-stage Yosys + ABC flow and the GE table
stages.refuses: a netlist with cells the table does not price (latches, flip-flops), a non-deterministic flow, a design over the depth budget

stages.what: `check/postsynth.py`: ls-sv and the scored netlist (Verilator) must agree on every vector of the budget
stages.refuses: any disagreement, x/z in ls-sv outputs, a netlist Verilator will not build; a rejection is a bug report

policies: **Combinational tasks only for now.** Clocked designs, registers and pipelines are refused until the sequential layer exists (Thomas, 2026-10-29).
**Where the tools split, the design is refused**, never decided for one side: Icarus, Xcelium, Verilator, Yosys and slang are compared, and a shape they read differently is a loud refusal (Thomas).

**Everything the proof and the score could read differently is refused exactly, before any proof is tried** (the x/z rules, the source gate), and the post-synthesis check is the backstop for the disagreements nobody has found.
**No other restrictions.** Beyond the per-task operator banlist and these safety gates, write any SystemVerilog ls-sv can load.
**Contestants may add features to ls-sv by pull request, and Thomas approves every such PR.** See 'How a refusal becomes allowed'.
**Proofs are symbolic and parametric** (for all N). `bv_decide` only for fixed-size subgoals and only once the checker can verify it; `native_decide` is banned in submissions.

groups.title: Stage `source`: one program for both tools
groups.intro: Yosys and slang (the frontend your proof is about) read the same file differently when it contains directives, attributes or pragma comments. The gate refuses those and hands every later stage one canonical text with all comments stripped.
groups.refused_example:
`ifdef SYNTHESIS
  assign y = a & b;     // Yosys defines SYNTHESIS, slang does not
`else
  assign y = a | b;
`endif
(* keep *) wire t;      // attribute: Yosys gives it a meaning
// synopsys translate_off

groups.title: Stage `source` and `fourstate`: no x or z may arise
groups.intro: ls-sv computes with unknown values like an IEEE simulator; Yosys treats them as don't-cares. Wherever an x reaches a decision the proved and the scored circuits can differ, and you choose where. Every SOURCE of an x or z is refused, exactly. A `casez` item may use `z` and `?`, a `casex` item `x`, `z`, `?`.
groups.write_ok:
always_comb begin
  casez (a[1:0])
    2'b1?: y = 1'b1;     // wildcard digit in a casez item: allowed
    default: y = 1'b0;
  endcase
end
groups.refused_example:
assign y = a[0] ? 1'bz : a[1];     // z literal
localparam logic [1:0] K = 2'd1 / 2'd0;   // constant division by zero is x
logic [3:0] m; ... m[{1'b1, a[1:0]}]     // index can leave the range: x
logic u; assign y = u ? a : b;           // u is undriven

groups.title: Stage `banlist`: the task's banned operators
groups.intro: A task bans the run-time operator that IS the task, plus whatever Yosys merges into the same cell (alumacc turns `+` and `-` chains into the cells of `*`). Constant arithmetic (parameters, genvar loops, index arithmetic over parameters and genvars) and comparisons stay allowed. Which operators are banned is per task: `add`, `mul` and `_example` ban `+ - * / % **`; `fdiv16` bans `/ % **`.
groups.write_ok:
for (genvar i = 0; i < N; i++) begin : g
  assign s[i] = a[i] ^ b[i] ^ c[i];     // gates, not +
  assign c[i+1] = (a[i] & b[i]) | (c[i] & (a[i] ^ b[i]));   // i+1 is constant arithmetic
end
groups.refused_example:
assign s = a + b + cin;          // run-time + in a task that bans it
assign y = a * b;                // run-time *
assign n = $countones(a);        // Yosys builds it from $add cells
assign p = arr.sum();            // array reduction = run-time +

groups.title: Stages `extract` and `design`: the language tier and the parameter list
groups.intro: The proof is about what the pinned extractor and the ls-sv loader accept. A construct they refuse fails here with the tier's own message. The top module's overridable parameters must be exactly the task's, by name and order, because the scoring script overrides them by name.
groups.write_ok: module band #(parameter int N = 4)(input logic [N-1:0] a, b, output logic [N-1:0] y);
groups.refused_example:
module band #(parameter int N = 4, parameter int M = 2)(...);   // an extra parameter
module band #(parameter bit [3:0] N = 4)(...);               // narrower than int: N = 16 reads as 0

groups.title: Stage `imports`: the proof file
groups.intro: The checker builds only SvGolf, the task modules and the evaluator; any other module is unaudited code outside the trusted base. One solution file in v0.
groups.write_ok:
import Submission.Design
import LeanModels.Sv.Ingest2
import SvGolf.Comb

groups.title: The trusted statement: interface, clocks, termination, function, range
groups.intro: The statement is a Lean `Prop` fixed by the task (`SvGolf/Task.lean`). A design that satisfies it must have exactly the task's ports, no edge-phase process, a completed run for every schedule and stimulus, and the task's function at every cycle, for every N in the range. These are not rules you can argue with: a design that breaks one has no proof of the statement, and the repository checks the refutations in `tests/*/negative/Refute.lean`.

groups.title: Stages `comparator`, `leanchecker`, `integrity`: the proof itself
groups.intro: The kernel must accept your theorem from the task's allowed axioms alone. Everything that would let a proof depend on something other than the kernel is refused.
groups.write_ok:
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by
  -- induction on bit indices, decide +kernel for fixed-size subgoals
  ...
groups.refused_example:
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by native_decide   -- trusts the compiler
theorem solution : Submission.Goal := by sorry
axiom cheat : Submission.Goal

groups.title: Stages `score` and `postsynth`: the scored netlist
groups.intro: The score is area in NAND2 gate equivalents and depth, measured on the pinned Yosys + ABC netlist. The post-synthesis check then simulates ls-sv and the scored netlist on the task's vector budget and rejects any difference; it is sampling, so a difference confined to a tiny input region can slip through, which is what the static rules above are for. A rejection here is a bug report: either ls-sv or Yosys is wrong.
groups.refused_example: always_ff @(posedge clk) y <= a & b;    // a flip-flop in the netlist: not priced

groups.title: Task authors: `task.json`
groups.intro: Mistakes in a task definition fail loudly so a typo cannot silently change the vector budget or the banlist.
groups.refused_example:
"banlist": {"operators": ["<<"]}     // unknown operator
"allow_bv_decide": true                  // refused until the comparator can verify it

never_summary: Anything the tools read differently (the policy: `P-NO-SILENT-PICK`): self-reading and alias-reading `always_comb`, narrow net actuals into wider net inputs, partly out-of-range part selects, bit-select indexes wider than 32 bits, context-width port actuals, initialized variables with a second writer.
Tool directives of any kind (`P-NO-TOOL-DIRECTIVES`): `ifdef SYNTHESIS, attributes, synthesis-pragma comments.

Delays, timing and randomness in a combinational task (`P-NO-TIME`, `P-DETERMINISM`); non-hardware constructs such as classes, strings, reals, dynamic memory, file I/O and `fork`/`join` (`P-SYNTHESIZABLE`).
Anything that lets a submission change what the checker trusts (`P-TRUSTED-BASE`): `sorry`, user axioms, `extern` / `implemented_by`, a player-supplied envelope.
lifting: Every refusal above has a state. `refused-now` means no change is planned. `later` names the prerequisite that has to exist first; when it exists, the refusal is lifted by a pull request.

**How to propose it.** Open a pull request against lean-surfaces that adds the feature to ls-sv (extractor, `LeanModels/Sv`), with differential cases against independent oracles (Xcelium pinned data, Icarus, Verilator, Yosys): a disagreement is fixed or declared, never ignored. Thomas approves every such PR.

**If the construct brings an x source** (a function local read before assignment, a latch that is never loaded, `always @*`), a rule in `score/fourstate.py` must land first or in the same PR; the post-synthesis check is the backstop, not the plan.

**For the checker's own rules** (the source gate, the banlist, the statement), changing a refusal changes what every earlier submission means: the PR must say so, and leaderboard entries record the lean-surfaces revision they were checked against.
**Update the register.** Add or edit the row in `docs/sv-refusals.json`, run `python3 tools/gen_sv_refusals.py --write`, and `--check` must pass.
limits: The post-synthesis check is sampling (fixed corners, task corners, harvested comparison constants, seeded random): a difference confined to a region no comparison constant selects can pass (`oob_rare.sv`, `zpair_add_rare.sv` pass it alone; the static rules are the only line there).

There is no sandbox: `import Lean` is allowed, so a Solution.lean can run `#eval` with checker privileges. The integrity snapshot is a tripwire, not a defence. Run untrusted submissions in a throwaway container.

The parameter's declared type is not pinned by the statement; the multi-point cross-check at the scoring point keeps the scored design one ls-sv and slang agree on, elsewhere the statement is about ls-sv's reading.
The banlist front check is heuristic (a variable copied from a loop counter counts as run-time); the Yosys backstop covers the scored points only.

The fourstate stage checks the SCORING POINT only (not the probe points) and filters `tri-state` warnings out of Yosys `check`. Its run-time index rule reasons from index TYPES: `a[i-1]` with a 2-bit `i` is a 32-bit index and is refused on any declared range (over-refusal), as is any procedural loop counter used as an index.

A gate hole not yet measured: x/z digits are exempt anywhere inside a casez/casex item EXPRESSION, not only as the item's own literal (`casez (a[1:0]) (a[0] == 1'bz) ? 2'b00 : 2'b01: ...` passes the gate). Whether ls-sv and Yosys then differ was not measured; do not rely on it.

A plain syntax error is reported by the gate as `preprocessor-skipped text` before the extractor or Yosys see it; `always @(*)` passes the gate (the `(*)` is exempt) and is refused later by the language tier.
`ARITH_PRIMITIVES` (`$alu $macc $macc_v2 $lcu $fa`) in the banlist backstop are dead entries: the backstop reads without `-icells`, so instantiating one fails earlier with `yosys failed`.

`--no-gate` in `score.py` and `postsynth.py` is a research flag: the result says `gated: false` and is not a svGolf score. Missing Verilator, make, a C++ compiler, Yosys or `svgolf-eval` is an infrastructure error (exit 2), never a rejection.
Open policy question: comparisons are not banned in `add` / `mul`; a carry written as a comparison is Yosys's own alu logic and scores lower depth than the proved ripple reference.
Open: must challenge proofs be parametric (for all N)? The README treats it as decided; `svgolf/PLAN.md` still lists it as a question for Thomas.

entries.trigger: `` `pragma protect begin ``
entries.why: A `` `pragma `` is a tool directive by definition: each tool acts on the pragma names it knows.

entries.tag: other directives: `` `line ``, `` `celldefine ``, `` `resetall ``, `` `begin_keywords ``; `` `default_nettype `` other than none | wire; a malformed `` `timescale ``
entries.trigger: `` `line 10 "x.sv" 0 ``;  `` `default_nettype uwire ``;  `` `timescale 1ns ``

entries.why: Yosys gives attributes (full_case, parallel_case, keep, nosync, keep_hierarchy, blackbox, ...) a synthesis meaning; slang and IEEE simulation give them none. `always @(*)` still passes the gate.

entries.trigger: // synopsys translate_off;  /* synthesis keep */;  // pragma foo;  and the words translate_off, translate_on, full_case, parallel_case anywhere in ANY comment
entries.why: Yosys's lexer reads these comments as directives; slang ignores comments. Refusing is a courtesy; STRIPPING every comment is the guarantee. A comment that merely names full_case is refused too (over-refusal).

entries.trigger: unique case (a[0]) ... endcase;  unique if (...) ... else ...;  unique0 case ...;  priority case ...
entries.why: Yosys turns unique into full_case + parallel_case, unique0 into parallel_case, priority into full_case (synthesis don't-cares); ls-sv runs the first matching arm. A unique case that never matches scores 0 GE.
entries.prerequisite: WP5: ls-sv turns a violated qualifier claim into a run-time error on the settled state so Terminates2 forces the proof obligation; the gate refusal goes once WP5 lands
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-28 (carry proof obligations) and 2026-10-29 (v0 refuses; WP5 deferred)

entries.tag: non-ASCII or control characters outside comments; a file that is not UTF-8
entries.trigger: string s = "héllo"; a form feed; a stray 0xFF byte
entries.why: Identifier and string lexing of non-ASCII text is each tool's business; the gate refuses rather than assume the tools agree (non-ASCII INSIDE a comment passes).

entries.tag: an unterminated block comment; `//` or `/*` inside a string or an escaped identifier; text slang skips (a syntax error)
entries.trigger: /* never closed;  string s = "// not a comment";  assign y = a & b @@ ;
entries.why: No comment boundary exists, or Yosys's lexer might see a comment that slang does not; skipped or disabled text may still be parsed by Yosys.

entries.tag: x, z or ? digits in a literal outside a casez/casex item wildcard
entries.trigger: 1'bz;  4'b10x0;  'x;  'z;  4'b1??0;  8'hz?  in an assign, an == operand, a plain case item, a localparam, a `case inside` item
entries.why: ls-sv computes with x/z like IEEE simulation (a z item never matches a known input); Yosys reads an x/z bit as a don't-care and drops it from comparisons: complementary items 2'b0z, 2'b1z match no input in ls-sv and EVERY input in Yosys.
entries.prerequisite: the x-taint feature: allow x sources but forbid x-tainted values from reaching non-monotone decisions; first measure the area gain of don't-cares on a real task
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-29: x/z literals and the fourstate stage stay in v0
entries.value_note: don't-care assignments (`'x`) to save area, via the x-taint feature

entries.tag: an x digit in a casez item
entries.why: Only z and ? are casez wildcards; an x bit in a casez item is NOT a wildcard and the two tools read it differently.
entries.prerequisite: as for x/z literals (x-taint feature)
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-29: x/z literals stay refused in v0

entries.tag: internal: the canonical text differs from the submitted token stream
entries.trigger: not triggerable by a design (a stripper bug)
entries.why: Fail closed: the gate validates its own stripping with slang.

match.text: internal: the canonical text still has

entries.tag: a run-time `+ - * / % **` in a task that bans it
entries.trigger: assign y = a + b;  a - b;  a * b;  a / b;  a % b;  a ** b;  with run-time operands
entries.why: The operator that IS the task, plus what Yosys merges into the same cell (alumacc: + and - chains become the cells of *). Constant arithmetic stays allowed. Which operators: tasks/*/task.json banlist.operators.

entries.tag: the same arithmetic in other forms: compound assignment, unary minus, ++ / --, array .sum() / .product(), $countones & co, run-time index arithmetic
entries.trigger: y += a;  -a;  x++;  arr.sum();  $countones(a);  a[j + 1];  x[sel*W +: W]
entries.why: Each builds the same $add / $sub / $mul / $neg cell. Procedural for-loop counters (k++) and constant arguments stay allowed. Yosys 0.53 cannot read .sum() at all, a later one may.

entries.tag: a banned operator hidden behind a constant-argument function call, in a generate branch the scoring point does not take, or behind a loop counter that is written
entries.trigger: function automatic logic [15:0] g(input int k); g = a / 16; endfunction  assign q = g(0);   for (int k...) begin k = int'(a[0]); ... end
entries.why: A call is constant only when its arguments are AND its body reads nothing but its own arguments and locals; Yosys silently ignores a write to a loop counter and folds the loop, simulation does not (the proof and the score then differ).
entries.notes: The loop-counter rule only bites for tasks that ban + or - (it works by treating the counter as run-time).

entries.tag: a design Yosys or slang cannot read at a backstop point
entries.trigger: syntax Yosys 0.53 lacks (arr.sum()); an undeclared identifier
entries.why: A design Yosys cannot read cannot be scored; the front check cannot walk what slang rejects. The banlist fails closed.

entries.tag: a constant with unknown bits: parameter, localparam, inline constant, constant function result, out-of-range constant select
entries.trigger: localparam logic [3:0] K = 4'd1 / 4'd0;  a constant function returning an unassigned local;  v[6 +: 4] on [7:0];  an enum member with an x value
entries.why: Constant division by zero is not banned as arithmetic but it is x: ls-sv computes with it, Yosys reads it as a don't-care.
entries.prerequisite: the x-taint feature
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-29: the fourstate stage stays in v0

entries.tag: a run-time index whose type can address outside the declared range
entries.trigger: logic [N-1:0] mem [3:0]; y = mem[i] with a 3-bit i (0..7 on [3:0]);  a signed index;  v[i +: 4] with a 3-bit i on [7:0]
entries.why: An out-of-range read is x. The rule reasons from the index TYPE alone (an unsigned w-bit index ranges 0..2^w-1): exact for the checker's purpose but it over-refuses indexes the design keeps in range by other means. Fix: declare a power-of-two range or narrow the index.
entries.prerequisite: the x-taint feature (and value-range reasoning on the index expression to narrow the over-refusal, a proposal)
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-29: the fourstate stage stays in v0
entries.notes: Over-refuses a[i-1] with a 2-bit i (typed 32-bit) and any procedural for-loop counter used as an index; the generate-for twin passes.

entries.trigger: always_comb begin for (int k = 0; k < N; k++) y[k] = a[k] & b[k]; end
entries.why: Documented gap: ls-sv does not load procedural loops today, and a PR that admits them should teach this rule loop bounds. The generate-for twin passes.
entries.prerequisite: none recorded; proposed prerequisite: ls-sv loads procedural loops AND rule (d) learns loop bounds
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-29: approved the refused-now and later classifications of the register

entries.trigger: (not triggered: a queue reports a fixed range; slang rejects a non-constant width)

entries.tag: any edge-phase process (always_ff, always @(posedge clk), an async-reset block), even with a dead clock
entries.trigger: always_ff @(posedge clk) s <= a ^ b;  clock tied low or undriven
entries.why: ls-sv runs every edge-phase process once per cycle whatever its clock holds, so a register on a clock nothing drives holds the right value in ls-sv and x in every simulator (0 GE in Yosys).
entries.prerequisite: the sequential layer: ls-sv models clock edges; the `Unclocked` requirement goes then
entries.decided_by: Thomas 2026-10-29: keep things combinatorial to begin with
entries.value_note: registered, pipelined and multi-cycle designs (serial multiplier, iterative divider)
entries.notes: Since WP-Q0 (2026-10-30) ls-sv itself refuses a dead, tied, gated, derived, register, internal-net, multiple or data-read clock and an internal asynchronous reset at the loader (gu-clock-source, gu-clock-reset, gu-clock-multiple, gu-clock-data-read in docs/sv-refusals.md), so a CLOCKED design that loads is single-clock and input-port-clocked. `Unclocked` stays the statement-level requirement of combinational tasks; the sequential statement (ClockedBy, svgolf/design/sequential/README.md) replaces it and the loader refusals are its loader-side twin.
